subject: literature
passage: Every winter afternoon, when the sun came low and thin through the arches of the Qissa Khwani Bazaar in Peshawar, Gul Rahim set out his books on a faded carpet and waited. He did not call to the passersby as the fruit sellers did; he held that a book which must be shouted for is not worth the reading. Students stopped, turned a page or two, and went on. A soldier once bought a volume of verse for its red binding and was gently advised to take a cheaper one with better poems. By evening Gul Rahim had generally sold nothing, and he would wrap the books again in their cloth, one by one, with the air of a man who has spent his day exactly as he wished.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To portray a bookseller whose principles matter more to him than making sales
choices.B: To show how a bookseller's refusal to advertise eventually brings him success
choices.C: To describe the ordinary trade of a bazaar's fruit sellers and its booksellers
choices.D: To suggest that a bookseller's gentle manner hides a growing bitterness

explanation.why: Gul Rahim refuses to shout for customers on principle, and he even talks a buyer into a cheaper book with "better poems." Though he "generally sold nothing," he packs up like "a man who has spent his day exactly as he wished." The passage portrays someone who values his ideas about books over making money.
explanation.A: Correct. His refusal to advertise, his advice to the soldier, and his contentment despite poor sales all show principles valued above profit.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says he "generally sold nothing," so his methods do not bring success.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The fruit sellers appear only once, as a contrast that shows Gul Rahim's character.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The last sentence shows contentment, not hidden bitterness.
